VALUE: The supplied official-source excerpt states that SDMX Cross-Domain Concepts support reuse in statistical data and metadata exchange and gives Observation Status as concept ID OBS_STATUS with codelist ID CL_OBS_STATUS as an example. It does not confirm exact concept scheme IDs or versions for all common concepts used here and does not confirm code mappings for Final, Provisional, or Survey estimate.

The supplied official-source excerpt confirms that the SDMX Global Registry includes a searchable codelist catalogue and codelist-detail functions. It does not confirm the detailed entries, versions, agencies, or code definitions for CL_FREQ, CL_OBS_STATUS, or other specific codelists relevant to this report.

The accepted codelists artifact includes candidate CL_FREQ codes M and A, but the supplied registry excerpt does not confirm the CL_FREQ item, agency, version, or code definitions, so M and A remain candidate frequency mappings pending production verification.

The supplied SDMX Glossary excerpt confirms OBS_STATUS and gives CL_OBS_STATUS as its associated codelist example. No supplied external evidence confirms exact CL_OBS_STATUS code values or definitions, so report status values are mapped to the governed local report-status codelist rather than to confirmed SDMX CL_OBS_STATUS codes.

The shared reference catalogue identifies COICOP and SDMX CL_COICOP_2018 as candidate sources for consumption-purpose classifications. The report states that the consumption divisions resemble COICOP but does not confirm the revision, and no official code-level COICOP evidence was supplied.

The shared reference catalogue identifies ISO 4217 as the standard to check for currency identity. The report states only that values are in local currency and explicitly says that the local currency is not named, so no ISO 4217 currency code can be assigned from the supplied evidence.

The supplied UN M49 excerpt shows country and area entries with numeric and alpha codes. The report does not state a reference area, so no REF_AREA field or area mapping is included in this operational codebook.

This codebook covers two distinct statistical structures: KF_SYNTH_CPI_DIVISION_MONTHLY for monthly CPI by consumption division and KF_SYNTH_HH_SPENDING_RESIDENCE_QUINTILE_ANNUAL for annual household spending by residence type and expenditure quintile.
Local codelist references are aligned to the accepted CODELISTS artifact: CL_LOCAL_CPI_DIVISION, CL_LOCAL_RESIDENCE, CL_LOCAL_EXPENDITURE_QUINTILE, CL_LOCAL_UNIT_MEASURE, and CL_LOCAL_REPORT_STATUS.

The exact SDMX concept scheme IDs and versions for common concepts such as FREQ, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE, UNIT_MEASURE, OBS_STATUS, BASE_PERIOD, ESTIMATION_TYPE, and STAT_UNIT were not confirmed by the supplied external evidence.
The exact SDMX CL_FREQ agency, version, and code definitions were not supplied. FREQ=M and FREQ=A are candidate standard mappings and must be verified before production automation.
The report status values Final and Provisional are mapped to governed local CL_LOCAL_REPORT_STATUS codes, not to confirmed SDMX CL_OBS_STATUS codes.
Survey estimate is modelled as ESTIMATION_TYPE using the governed local CL_LOCAL_REPORT_STATUS code SURVEY_ESTIMATE and is not treated as an SDMX observation-status code.

The CPI source unit string Index, 2023=100 is mapped to the governed local unit code IDX_2023_100. BASE_PERIOD=2023 is retained only as an optional derived CPI qualifier for template clarity, not as a replacement for the governed unit code.
Consumption divisions are local because the report says they resemble COICOP but the revision is not confirmed.
The local currency is not named, so household spending values cannot be mapped to a confirmed ISO 4217 currency code.
The report does not state a reference area or country; REF_AREA is not included and remains a production gap if geographic identification is required.
Residence type categories Urban and Rural are not mapped to a standard degree-of-urbanisation codelist because the report does not define classification criteria.
The report shows only lowest and highest expenditure quintiles. Intermediate quintile codes are not created without evidence.
